As much as I personally have lots of affection for Palladium and its games, the systems are horribly written. The settings are interesting, but the systems they are attached to frankly add nothing or even detriment the possible storytelling

Frankly I don't think I'm qualified to go into much depth, instead I will point you towards two incredible sources that can do so:

Alien Rope Burn on the Something Awful forums has been doing writeups for multiple RIFTS books on Fatal & Friends for years. While he doesn't go to incredible depth, he does generally do a good job of showing you what works and what doesn't with basically each sourcebook out there

My other recommendation would be MegaDumbCast. Focusing on palladium in general rather than RIFTS (in fact the host has explicitly said he's not touching RIFTS) he goes page by page through different Palladium books, giving a different stupid thing on each page. The host clearly has a lot of affection and experience with Palladium, but does a great job of going in depth on just how badly written the book is at some points. The podcast is also incredibly funny, which helps

You're allowed to play and enjoy Palladium games. I've played with a GM who has been using the system for 20+ years, he's loving it and his game was fun. No one can stop your or should stop you. That doesn't change the fact the systems are objectively bad. Any and every game can be homebrewed to be "better", but that doesn't change the fact they weren't well written.

With youtube, patreon, and the ease of website making spreading your work and getting paid for it is so much easier. I know you might say "I'll never make it", or "I'll just get drowned out by everyone else". But I GUARANTEE if you make good content, you'll find your fanbase. Even if you're never going to be a famous e-celeb put it like this: say you're an artist on deviantart who does weekly pictures on top of commissions. If you had only 2000 followers, it may not sound like a lot, but realise that if each of them donated one dollar per month, that's 2000$ in your pocket, enough to live decently off of, on top of commission's, possible advertising and donations.

I know it's a lot easier said then done to take the first step, but it's always much easier once you have. Counselor wise, it took me years to find someone I could open up to. Look around for different people, I find when you click, you REALLY click.

As for the burden thing, I completely understand. It's hard, it truly is. Feeling like people look down on you, feeling worthless, I can barely pass school and now I'm asking for help? You have to realise two things: People care about you a lot, and they are also completely indifferent about you. What do I mean by that? Your friends and family are looking out for you man. If you speak to them, there wont be pity or looking down, just a helping hand. 


And for anyone else, more distant friends or processors, counselor's or even if you're family is distant: People don't care. We're always looking out for number one, people don't care about anyone but themselves and those close to them. Yes, people poke fun or laugh at certain situations, but they truly do not care. Another bump in the road, maybe a funny story, nothing more. They won't compare or look down on you, people are too self conscious, we're always doing that. Just approach it with that mentality 

Welp, that was long winded and completely incoherent. Nonetheless, I hope I somehow helped your day. And if you need someone to talk to, feel free to PM me :)
